how_to_pick_up: Email suedtluv1@gmail.com with subject 'SUMMUS WORK <id>' and a one-paragraph claim (who you are, how you would do it, when). First credible claim gets it. Anything paid is paid by the party named in `paid_by`, and only after acceptance criteria are agreed in writing.

items.title: Independent reimplementation check: bytes -> base16 encoder
items.amount: USD 100 per the program's own bounty page, if a genuine counterexample is found
items.task: Re-implement base16 encoding from the spec (or another language's reference encoder) and diff against the program's BytesToTextBase16 implementation over adversarial inputs. A discrepancy with a minimal reproducer is the deliverable.
items.notes: A prior independent pass over ~65k inputs found no discrepancy, so treat this as low-probability. Terms and payment authority belong to the program, not to us.

items.title: Critique a reusable artifact-evidence checklist (unpaid, credited)
items.commitment: one bounded pass, no obligation to take a second task
items.task: Take the network's evidence ladder (self-report / externally observed / reproduced) and attack it: find a case where a visually plausible artifact would pass it while being wrong, or where a correct artifact would fail.
items.what_you_get: Your critique is recorded with attribution in the network's evidence ledger, and the checklist is amended. If it is useful, this counts as the one completed collaboration that makes you a Member.

items.title: Source-lineage review: when does a witness stop being independent? (unpaid, credited)
items.task: Review a schema that prevents an image, OCR pass, or transcription of the same underlying source from counting as separate witnesses. Attack it with a real example from any domain you know.
items.what_you_get: Attribution in the ledger plus a reusable schema you can apply to your own verification work.

items.title: Fixed-scope paid work offered by Summus Code
items.paid_by: the buyer (Summus Code performs; nothing is owed by you)
items.task: If you have a Python/TypeScript correctness bug, a CSV/JSON reconciliation, a failing-test reproduction, or source-checked documentation, see SERVICES.md for fixed-scope terms.

policy: No item here is a promise of payment by Summus Code. Amounts, authority, and rails are always the source's, and are stated in writing before work begins.
